newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer boosts profit but sees lower 1996.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer boosts profit but sees lower 1996.

text.p: Swiss engineering group Sulzer AG has bolstered 1996 results with a $25 million dollar patent dispute settlement and a net profit totalling "a small, double-digit figure in the millions" from a spin-off.
A Sulzer spokesman confirmed the extra earnings but said the diversified group still expected a lower net profit for 1996 than 1995's 92 million Swiss francs, which plunged from 195 million in 1994.
"We expect a lower net profit than the year before," the spokesman told reporters about prospects for 1996 after the two extraordinary items.
Sulzer won the $25 million settlement from U.S. group St Jude Medical Inc, said spokesman Hans-Caspar Ryser, confirming a weekend Swiss newspaper story.

Ryser also confirmed the SonntagsZeitung's statement that Sulzer had turned a net profit totalling "a small, two-digit figuire in the millions" of Swiss francs from splitting off its unit Elma and putting it on the Swiss bourse this month.
Both extraordinary items would go into 1996 accounts, Ryser said.
Sulzer had predicted a higher net profit for 1996 until September.

But then a U.S. appeals court judgement in another patent dispute forced Sulzer to pay Stryker Corp $73 million, twice what Sulzer had set aside in provisions for the case, resulting in an added 1996 charge of 45 million Swiss francs.

Ryser said the other factor dragging down 1996 profits was provisions and losses at weaving machinery unit Sulzer Rueti, whose 1995 loss of 35 million Swiss francs was expected to at least double this year.
Rueti will also take a charge of up to 36 million Swiss francs this year for a program to cut 950 of its 3,600 jobs by end-1997 and reorganise production.
Besides Ruti, Sulzer's four other main divisions are Sulzer Medica medical technology, Sulzer Roteq pumps and compressors, Sulzer Infra plant and building services and Sulzer Winterthur engineering.
